title: The Bridge Protocol

canonical_node.axiom: No physics-theology mapping is canonical merely because it is beautiful, emotionally resonant, rhetorically powerful, or spiritually useful; it must pass through four explicit layers: physical, structural, theological, and epistemic.
definitions: Physics Claim: A statement about the physical world, accountable to physics, using language like measured, modeled, observed, mathematically described, experimentally supported, standard interpretation, contested interpretation.

Structural Claim: A domain-neutral pattern abstracted from the physics, stated without religious language, using language like structurally resembles, instantiates the pattern of, behaves like, has the formal features of, preserves the relation.

Theological Mapping: A claim that the structural pattern corresponds to a theological concept, using language like maps to, corresponds to, illuminates, gives physical form to, provides a structural analogy for, may be read as.

Character Claim: A synthetic claim about what the mapped structure reveals about God, Christ, sin, grace, judgment, love, truth, or human nature, using language like the framework reads this as, this supports the portrait of, this contributes to the claim that, within the Theophysics system, this means.
Stress Properties: Physical features that do not obviously fit the theological reading, which must be named in every mapping.
Rival Readings: At least one non-theological or alternative reading that must be acknowledged.
Claim Status Labels: Measured, Modeled, Structural, Analogical, Isomorphic, Theological, Synthetic, Homiletic, Speculative, Rejected.
derivation: The framework's power and vulnerability lie in the movement from measured physical property to structural pattern to theological meaning to character claim.
If the bridge is too loose, it becomes devotional metaphor; if too hard, it overclaims proof.
Therefore, a mapping becomes canonically usable only when it passes through four layers: Physical, Structural, Theological, Epistemic.
Each layer must be explicit, and the final claim must be labeled with a status.
Forbidden moves (physics smuggling, metaphor denial without formal burden, category collapse, cherry-picked property selection, one-way confirmation) weaken the framework and must be flagged.

A bridge is canonically strong only if it passes seven tests: Physical Boundedness, Structural Extraction, Relation Preservation, Bidirectional Pressure, Stress Properties, Rival Readings, Claim Status.
The canonical bridge template requires stating physical claim, structural pattern, theological mapping, stress test, claim status, and canonical sentence.

The worked example (Gravity/Grace) demonstrates that gravity does not prove grace but supplies a measured physical pattern that can be mapped to one aspect of grace, provided the mapping is limited and not inflated.
canonical_node.action: Apply the Bridge Protocol to all physics-theology mappings in the framework, ensuring each passes the four layers, seven tests, and is labeled with a claim status. Use the canonical bridge template for each law, and start with the strongest three mappings: Gravity/Grace, Strong Force/Love, Thermodynamics/Judgment and Need for External Rescue.
boundary: This protocol does not claim that physics alone can prove theological claims.
It does not allow physics prestige to make theological claims feel proven when only an analogy has been established.
It does not treat physics, metaphysics, theology, and rhetoric as the same kind of claim.
It does not permit cherry-picking only properties that fit the theology; stress properties must be named.
It does not permit one-way confirmation; failure conditions must be included.
It does not call a bridge canonical until it passes all seven tests.
test: Physical Boundedness: The physical claim is specific and not inflated.
Structural Extraction: The pattern is stated without theological words.
Relation Preservation: The mapping preserves relationships, not just vibes.
Bidirectional Pressure: The theology interprets the physics, but the physics also constrains the theology.
Stress Properties: Misfitting or dangerous properties are named.
Rival Readings: At least one non-theological or alternative reading is acknowledged.
Claim Status: The final claim is labeled as proof, model, analogy, formal isomorphism, synthesis, or devotional use.

dg1_dependencies: Physics claims must be accountable to standard physics.
Theological concepts must be grounded in theological interpretation or doctrine.
The framework's existing Ten Laws are subject to audit under this protocol.
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a rigorous method for evaluating and canonizing physics-theology mappings, preventing both loose analogy and overclaimed proof, and making the framework auditable.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the ability to make meaningful theological mappings from physics while maintaining epistemic humility and avoiding overclaim.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this protocol, the framework risks collapsing into either devotional metaphor with physics vocabulary or overclaimed proof that physics proves theology, undermining its credibility and internal conscience.
dg5_translation_registers: Physics register: measured, modeled, observed, mathematically described, experimentally supported.
Structural register: structurally resembles, instantiates the pattern of, behaves like, has the formal features of, preserves the relation.
Theological register: maps to, corresponds to, illuminates, gives physical form to, provides a structural analogy for, may be read as.
Epistemic register: proof, model, analogy, formal isomorphism, synthesis, devotional use.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Adopt as canonical method for auditing all physics-theology mappings; apply to all Ten Laws.

overstatement_risks: The protocol itself could be seen as establishing that physics can prove theology if not applied carefully.
The worked example might be taken as proof of grace rather than as an analogy.
The term 'isomorphic' is used sparingly but could be overused if not strictly defined.
kill_conditions: If the protocol is ignored and mappings are made without passing the seven tests.
If the protocol is used to claim that physics proves theology, violating its own boundaries.
If stress properties and rival readings are omitted from canonical mappings.
risk.lean_target: A formal system for evaluating physics-theology mappings, potentially implementable in Lean, to check that each mapping satisfies the required structural relations and claim status.

plain_summary: This document establishes a protocol for legitimately mapping physics to theology, requiring explicit layers (physical, structural, theological, epistemic), seven tests, and claim status labels to prevent overclaim and loose analogy. It provides a worked example (gravity/grace) and mandates applying the protocol to all laws.
